tuning_discipline: k chosen as the smallest k whose cv_auc_mean is within 0.002 of the best k's cv_auc_mean, over the 4 CV folds only. All holdout numbers come from run_standard_eval and are reported for the record; the holdout was never used to choose k, features, or anything else. Univariate screening also uses the 4 CV folds only. Seed 108 everywhere.

method.univariate: per-feature single-column AUC via ml.evaluation.iter_folds(feature_subset=[f], preprocess='raw'); score = raw feature value on test rows; AUC = max(auc, 1-auc) applied to the mean raw AUC across the 4 CV folds, sign recorded ('+' = higher value -> higher P(beat))
method.lgbm_gain: gain importance of the fixed LightGBM {'num_leaves': 63, 'learning_rate': 0.05, 'n_estimators': 300, 'feature_fraction': 0.8, 'bagging_fraction': 0.8, 'bagging_freq': 1, 'min_data_in_leaf': 200, 'num_threads': 2, 'random_state': 108, 'verbose': -1} fit on fold 2026-06 train (raw preprocess)
method.permutation: sklearn permutation_importance of that model on fold 2026-06 test (33,874 rows), n_repeats=3, scoring=roc_auc, seed 108
method.redundancy: |spearman rho| > 0.9 on a 100,000-row sample (seed 108), *_isnan excluded; clusters are connected components, representative = best combined rank
method.combined_rank: average of the three descending ranks (univariate AUC deviation from 0.5, LGBM gain, permutation mean); top-k subsets take the best-ranked non-redundant features

selected.rule: smallest k with cv_auc_mean within 0.002 of the best k (best k=10, cv_auc_mean=0.530695); chosen by cv_auc_mean only, never holdout

rationale: The top-10 combined-rank subset is dominated by 4 long momentum, 2 volatility, 2 delivery, 1 trend/location, 1 short momentum; the strongest single feature is mom_12_1 (univariate AUC 0.5293, sign +). Redundancy is heavy: 9 clusters at |spearman rho|>0.9 (e.g. cs_rank_deliv_z/deliv_pct_z_20; cs_rank_turnover/log_turnover; cs_rank_vol_20/vol_20; dist_200dma/ret_126d), so each cluster contributes one representative to the subset. The elimination curve is flat past a small k: best cv_auc_mean 0.5307 at k=10, and k=10 is already within 0.002 of it (cv 0.5307), so the extra features buy almost nothing. k was chosen on cv_auc_mean only; the harness-reported holdout for the selected subset is 0.5219 on beat_mkt_20d and 0.5327 on up_5d, quoted for the record, never used to choose. Dead weight (20 features) is concentrated in features that are near-random univariately, carry <1% of LGBM gain and have zero/negative permutation importance: gap_pct, close_pos_in_range, range_pct, rsi_2, dist_sma_5, ret_1d, flag_below_200dma, mom_12_1_isnan, log_ret_1d, deliv_pct_sma_20_isnan, ret_126d_isnan, dist_sma_50_isnan.... Most *_isnan availability indicators add nothing once the value columns (or their representatives) are present, with the partial exception of the long-history indicators that proxy listing age early in the sample; none make the selected subset on merit. For the 5-year run I would carry the selected 10-feature subset plus at most the next 5-10 combined-rank features for re-checking (long-horizon returns get a full history there, so ret_252d/mom_12_1-type features deserve a re-audit), and drop the flagged redundant twins and the dead-weight list outright. Delivery-based features and volatility/liquidity ranks should be kept as a family (one representative each) since they are the main non-price information in the dataset.
